rows.evidence: Q1: Data and Method / Results - own monitoring of groundwater levels in wells twice monthly 2008-2010 plus soil sampling in four farmlands and shelterbelts. Q2: Results 'Variation of groundwater level', Figure 2 and Conclusions - groundwater level in the drip-irrigated oasis declined on average 0.5 m/yr (0.25 m/yr in conclusions) over 2008-2010 and was 1.0-1.3 m deeper in irrigation season; authors relate this to implementation of large-scale drip irrigation, with intro noting water-saving irrigation produces no deep percolation and reduces return flow. Q6: Groundwater monitoring and Results - 11 wells distributed across Kalamiji Oasis, decline reported for the oasis irrigation zone, not a single plot. Q8: Discussion - groundwater decline 'suspected' to result from drip irrigation and stated to need further monitoring to be confirmed; result described as only possibly related ('may be related'); only 2 years of observations.
rows.notes: Attribution of the groundwater decline to drip irrigation is tentative and confounded: the authors note the saved water was used to irrigate ~2230 ha of newly reclaimed land and that farmers pump groundwater for supplemental irrigation, which could itself cause the seasonal drawdown. There is no direct flood-vs-drip comparison of recharge; return flow or deep percolation is not measured (Q4 no). Only one method (well monitoring) is used for the groundwater result (Q3 no). Four farmlands of different soil texture are in a single oasis and climate, and decline is reported only as an oasis average (Q5 no). No requirement stated for the effect (Q7 no). No dispersion measure for the decline rate; the reported rate is inconsistent (0.5 vs 0.25 m/yr) between abstract/results and conclusions (Q9 no).

notes: Full text appears complete. Internal inconsistency in the reported groundwater decline rate (0.5 m/yr in abstract and results; 0.25 m/yr in French abstract and conclusions). The study's main strength is on soil salinity in shelterbelts vs farmlands; the groundwater-drip link is observational and acknowledged by the authors as unconfirmed.
